## Modern Accounting Recruitment

The traditional campus recruiting playbook — meet-and-greet events, summer internships, full-time offers — still works but is no longer sufficient. Firms must also compete for lateral talent and non-traditional candidates.

### Campus Recruiting Evolution

| Traditional Approach | Modern Approach |
|---|---|
| Target top 20 accounting programs | Expand to 50+ schools including community colleges |
| Meet-and-greet events | Virtual open houses + in-person experiences |
| Summer internships only | Year-round micro-internships, co-ops |
| Offer after internship | Earlier commitment with flexible start dates |
| GPA-focused screening | Skills and culture fit assessment |

### The Internship-to-Hire Pipeline

The accounting internship is still the primary hiring pipeline:

- 90% of Big Four entry-level hires come through internships
- Interns who receive offers accept at 85% rate
- Best-in-class internship programs include client exposure, mentorship, and social connection

#### Building a Great Internship Program

- Meaningful work : Interns should work on real engagements, not just filing
- Mentorship : Assign a staff mentor AND a partner champion
- Social connection : Team events, cohort bonding, firm culture exposure
- Performance feedback : Mid-point and final evaluations with development areas
- Competitive pay : $28-$38/hour depending on market

### Lateral Recruitment

Experienced hire recruitment requires different tactics:

| Level | Where They Come From | What They Want | How to Reach Them |
|---|---|---|---|
| Senior | Other firms, industry | Better work-life, interesting clients | LinkedIn, referrals |
| Manager | Other firms, controllers | Partnership potential, compensation | Recruiters, networking |
| Senior Manager | Competing firms, industry VP | Clear partner path, meaningful clients | Targeted outreach |
| Partner | Competing firms (with book) | Platform, economics, culture | Senior leadership outreach |

### Diversity in Accounting Recruitment

The accounting profession lacks diversity:

- 75% of CPAs are white; 4% are Black
- Women make up 62% of staff but only 23% of partners

Improving diversity:

- Recruit from HBCUs and HSIs
- Scholarship and fellowship programs
- Inclusive internship experiences
- Diverse interview panels
- Mentorship and sponsorship for underrepresented groups

### Retention After Hiring

The first 2 years have the highest attrition:

- Year 1: 15% turnover (primarily culture fit issues)
- Year 2: 25% turnover (industry exits for better pay/hours)
- Year 3-5: 20% turnover (manager-level departures for industry roles)

Retention levers by level:

- Staff : Mentoring, study support, social connection
- Senior : Specialization opportunities, interesting clients
- Manager : Partnership clarity, compensation, flexibility
- Senior Manager : Equity participation, leadership responsibility
